assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and credit amplification form a core part of how macroeconomists understand business cycles, financial crises and policy. The Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism was developed into a large quantitative literature on financial frictions and intermediaries, and it shaped post-2008 policy thinking.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the clearest originators of the collateral-constraint cycle mechanism. Gertler's work on the financial accelerator (with Bernanke) and on intermediary frictions extends it and gives a third strong contributor. Gilchrist is more empirical and was left out. Bernanke's earlier prize overlaps with the accelerator strand, so credit allocation needs care.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers are from 1997 and earlier, with more than 25 years of confirmation, extension and policy use. The 2022 prize for banking and financial crises leaves room for this complementary macro-finance contribution, but it is a related area.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize (Bernanke, Diamond, Dybvig) and with the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist accelerator
Whether the committee would prefer a narrower two-person prize (Kiyotaki and Moore) over adding Gertler
Gertler also appears under B012, so there may be competing uses of his credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law and finance created a major research programme linking legal institutions, investor protection and financial development. It had very wide impact on corporate finance, comparative institutions and development, and it changed how economists measure and compare institutions across countries.
assessment.attribution: The 1997-98 papers by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny are the core. Vishny is credited in the foundational work, but the prize limit is three. Shleifer's wider contributions (behavioural finance, corporate governance) strengthen his case, while La Porta and Lopez-de-Silanes are central to the legal-origins data and agenda.
assessment.maturity: About 30 years of replication, extension and critique. The literature is mature, which makes the lasting value assessable.
uncertainties: The legal-origins identification strategy and its causal claims have been contested
The four-name credit set exceeds the prize limit, so the choice of three involves judgement about Vishny
Non-scientific controversies around some credited individuals are not evidence here and are not weighed

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson and Tabellini built the modern theory and empirics of how constitutions, electoral rules and political institutions shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. Besley's work on state capacity and accountability adds to this. It is a coherent, foundational programme that has become standard in political economy.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the central pair, through their 2000 book and many papers. Besley is a co-pioneer with a distinct line on state capacity and political agency. The three-name credit set is natural and mostly non-overlapping with the 2024 laureates, though the field overlap with institutions and growth needs care.
assessment.maturity: The work spans 1990-2020, with a long record of empirical testing and extension, so maturity is high.
uncertainties: Conceptual overlap with the 2024 prize for institutions and prosperity
Mixed empirical robustness for some constitutional-effects estimates
Whether the committee would give Besley's state-capacity work equal weight with the Persson-Tabellini core

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underlies modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice, including inflation targeting, rules and DSGE models. Its influence on policy and on macroeconomic modelling is very large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is widely diffused across Calvo, Taylor, Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans, Smets-Wouters, Gali and Woodford. Woodford's Interest and Prices gave the integrated theory, Gali and co-authors the canonical empirical and theoretical NK Phillips curve and policy analysis, and Taylor the rule and staggered contracts. Any three-person selection leaves out important contributors (Calvo, CEE), which is a significant weakness.
assessment.maturity: More than 30 years of development with extensive use in policy. The framework is fully mature, but it is also being challenged and extended (heterogeneity, the zero lower bound).
uncertainties: A diffuse credit set makes the three-name selection contestable
Whether the committee would prefer recognising the framework through some different combination
Possible overlap in credit for Gertler with B007

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity, selection and the gains from trade changed trade theory and empirics. It explained the exporter premium and the productivity effects of trade liberalisation, and it became the workhorse for micro-data-based trade analysis. It is a clear step beyond the new trade theory recognised in 2008.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the single most influential paper. Helpman contributed through the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work on exports versus FDI and a long line on trade and firms. Redding has major quantitative-spatial and firm-trade work but is a later-generation contributor. Bernard, Eaton-Kortum and others are not credited here, which leaves some attribution doubt.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of confirmation and extensions. Mature.
uncertainties: Credit may extend beyond the listed names (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum, Yeaple)
Overlap with the 2008 trade prize in subject area
Whether Helpman is better placed under B013 or B026

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural estimation of demand with differentiated products (BLP), and the Ericson-Pakes framework for dynamic industry models, turned industrial organisation into a quantitative discipline. The tools are used in antitrust, merger review and many applied fields, and have been extended well beyond IO.
assessment.attribution: Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes (1995) is the core of the demand-estimation strand, with Pakes as the clear intellectual leader across dynamic models (Ericson-Pakes, Olley-Pakes). Bresnahan's earlier work and others in the credited list are important but separable.
assessment.maturity: Nearly 30 years of use and refinement, including large practical impact on policy and a mature identification literature.
uncertainties: Credit split between the demand-estimation and dynamic-models strands
Whether the committee sees this as method or as substantive discovery
Seven credited names show wide attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the empirical analysis of trade shocks (the China shock) reshaped understanding of labour-market polarisation, wage inequality and the distributional effects of globalisation. The work is empirically rich and highly policy-relevant.
assessment.attribution: Autor-Levy-Murnane on tasks, Katz-Murphy and Goldin-Katz on skill demand, and Autor-Dorn-Hanson on trade shocks. Acemoglu and Restrepo's task-based theory, and Goldin's 2023 prize on women's labour, mean the committee must separate this from earlier recognition. Katz's contribution is long-running but partly overlaps with Goldin's recognised work.
assessment.maturity: Skill-biased change and polarisation are well established. The China shock results have been replicated and debated for about a decade, so they are reasonably confirmed but not fully settled.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 and 2023 prizes in the task and skill-demand themes
Debate over the size and persistence of China-shock effects
Hanson versus Dorn in the credit set

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run, tax-record-based measurement of top incomes and wealth changed the empirical basis of inequality research and public debate worldwide. The measurement contribution is large, and the Piketty-Saez series and the later distributional national accounts are widely used.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the originators of the top-income series, and Zucman extended this to wealth and offshore holdings. Atkinson (deceased) was a key precursor, so intellectual priority is shared. The credit largely rests on data construction, and the theoretical claims in Capital in the Twenty-First Century are contested.
assessment.maturity: Top-income work has about 20 years of use and replication. The wealth-tax and offshore-wealth estimates are more recent and still debated.
uncertainties: Contested methodology for wealth-concentration and distributional-accounts estimates
Whether the committee treats measurement as discovery equal to theory-based contributions
Zucman's relative recency compared with the other two
